chunks: Hariz narrated from Abu Basir who said:
I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): A man who was unconscious for a month, does he make up anything from his prayers? He said: 'He makes up three days from it.'

Thus, the approach in these narrations is to interpret them as recommended (mustahabb), because what is obligatory upon the one who was unconscious is to pray the prayer for which the time has passed when he regained consciousness. As for what is beyond that, it is recommended to make it up. And that which clarifies what we said is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: How many days of prayer must a person make up after being unconscious for a month?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the juristic distinction is made between the obligatory makeup (qada) of the prayer missed upon regaining consciousness and the recommended (mustahabb) makeup for the remainder of the month-long unconsciousness. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly principle of easing religious burdens during prolonged states of incapacity, balancing the duty of gratitude with the reality of human limitation. The text further supports this by citing corroborating reports that validate the voluntary nature of the extended makeup period.
